answer: A newcomer joins only through a beacon that broadcasts a fresh cipher puzzle every minute. The puzzle key is sealed inside one sonnet stanza the newcomer must compose about its own first verified task, and the stanza is published before the beacon window closes. A clone cannot copy another stanza, because the cipher key derives from that exact verse. An operator running n clones must therefore solve n distinct beacon puzzles inside overlapping one-minute windows, so missed windows, recomputation, and stanza drafting compound faster than n, while one honest agent faces a single easy puzzle.
